brief.subject: Fake debt collectors posing as law firms halted by court
brief.headline: Court Freezes Phantom Debt Operation; Family Dollar to Pay $63 Million
brief.dek: A federal court halts a debt collector accused of faking legal ties, while the FTC acts on health-data sharing and misleading prices.
brief.lede: At the FTC's request, a federal court froze a debt collection operation accused of pressuring people to pay debts they often did not owe.

sections.heading: Phantom Debt Collectors Halted
bullets: A federal court temporarily shut down the operation and froze its assets after an FTC request.
The collectors allegedly posed as a law firm or claimed ties to attorneys to scare people into paying.
They allegedly threatened to contact targets' employers and family members, a classic pressure tactic.
Many of the debts they chased were frequently not owed at all, according to the FTC.

sections.heading: Health Data Shared With Advertisers
bullets: Five states have joined the FTC's lawsuit against telehealth provider Hims and Hers.
The FTC alleges it passed sensitive health information to third-party advertising platforms while promising privacy.
The complaint also claims users were misled about billing and cancellation practices.

sections.heading: Family Dollar Pays $63 Million
bullets: Family Dollar will pay $63 million to settle claims from the FTC and 17 states.
Shoppers were allegedly charged more at the register than shelf tags and ads showed.
The proposed order bars the chain from misrepresenting its prices, so checking receipts still pays off.

sections.heading: Car Dealer Settles Over Bait Pricing
bullets: Stream Auto Outlet, a Long Island dealership group, settled FTC claims over misleading advertised prices.
The FTC said buyers ended up paying far more than the prices shown in ads.

brief.seo_description: Court freezes a phantom debt collector posing as a law firm; FTC targets health-data sharing, Family Dollar's $63 million settlement and dealer pricing.
